title: Wars Need More Than Two Armies
lesson: A war with one reason (an angry king) is a tantrum, not a war: nobody marches for it. Give every side its own reason worth the cost: something to gain, something to fear, a claim, a promise to an ally. Then let it start by mistake, because every side was sure the others would back down. Nobody thinks they're the villain.

voice.direction: The same lab host, like someone walking a general through a war room at night. The hook is flat and certain. 'Two armies, one angry king' is the cliché; 'a tantrum, not a war' lands dry. The rules are crisp, two beats each, each side's reason said as if it were obviously right. 'Nobody here wants this war' is quiet; 'All three are wrong' drops. The comment ask is playful.

lines.text: Nobody sends a million soldiers to die for an angry king.
Meet the Ruin War. It hasn't started yet.
The lazy version: two armies, one angry king.
Ten years of shouting. Nobody marches.
One angry king is a tantrum, not a war.
Real wars need reasons on every side. Four rules. The fifth is the twist.
One: something to gain. Red needs the ruin's harbour.
Two: fear. Blue can't let Red hold it.
Three: a claim. Gold's prince says it's his by birth.
Four: allies. Blue swore to stand with Gold.
Run it again. Ten years. Three armies, one ruin.
Rule five? Nobody here wants this war.
Each side is sure the others will blink. All three are wrong.
So give every side a reason worth the cost.
Show what each side wants. Nobody thinks they're the villain.
What would finally push your kingdom into war?
Part 36 of 50. Follow for part 37: big armies still lose.

shots.purpose: Close EP35's loop (three standards were planted round the ruin on 'two armies are never enough') and stop the scroll.
shots.visual: Golden hour over the Builders' ruin: three camps round it (red tents and standard west, blue north-east, gold south), their armies standing in front of the tents, and four coloured threads strung from the camps' pins to a knot on a tall war pin stuck in the ruin, glowing flashpoint lime, with one thread braided blue and gold between two camps. A MILLION SOLDIERS / FOR ONE ANGRY KING? from frame 0, each line pulsing on its word (NOT ONE KING · 3 SIDES · 4 REASONS at the knot). Then the field card: THE RUIN WAR · A WAR · NOT YET · SIDES: three, all sure they're right.
shots.camera: From the south-south-west (az 340, el 27, fov 20), pulling slowly back.

layers.midground: the knot, the threads, the camps

shots.onScreenText: A MILLION SOLDIERS / FOR ONE ANGRY KING? · FIELD CARD NO. 011 · THE RUIN WAR
shots.transition: Olive block wipe into the lazy version.
shots.music: Council: a ticking clock, plucked fifths, the theme on a muted trumpet; a hit on 'angry'.

shots.purpose: The lazy version: two armies, one angry king.
shots.visual: A wipe to two camps only (Red and Blue), no knot, one red thread (anger) strung from Red's camp to Blue's. TWO ARMIES / ONE ANGRY KING. The war room strip slides in under the world (RED: the king is angry; BLUE: nothing; GOLD absent; NO WAR); the sim bar arrives (ARMIES 02, REASONS 01) and RUN is pressed.
shots.camera: Cut close on Red's camp, pulling back along the anger thread to Blue's.
shots.onScreenText: TWO ARMIES · ONE ANGRY KING · THE WAR ROOM
shots.transition: A cut to the whole Isle on 'run'.

shots.purpose: Run the lazy version: ten years of shouting and nobody marches.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; YEAR 0→10; on 'Nobody' both camps strike their tents, the standards sink, the armies go home and the anger thread goes slack and reels back. 10 YEARS / OF SHOUTING / NOBODY MARCHES. ARMIES 2→0, REASONS 1→0; both verdicts read NOT WORTH IT.

shots.purpose: The punchline: one angry king is a tantrum, not a war.
shots.visual: Gloom: JUST A TANTRUM · 1 REASON · 0 ARMIES · NO WAR, over the empty camps.
shots.camera: Wide, the pull-back easing to a stop.
shots.onScreenText: JUST A TANTRUM · 1 REASON · 0 ARMIES · NO WAR

shots.purpose: Re-hook: the thesis, four rules, one locked.
shots.visual: REWIND to three camps with their armies and no threads (NO REASONS). REAL WARS / NEED REASONS; then the checklist PULL THE THREADS, row 5 locked (the twist).
shots.onScreenText: REAL WARS NEED REASONS · PULL THE THREADS 0/5
shots.music: Muster, bare (a field snare); a riser into 'the twist'.

graphics.kicker: THE RUIN WAR · WHY THEY MARCH
graphics.title: PULL THE THREADS

shots.purpose: Rule 1: something to gain (interests and resources).
shots.visual: Close on Red's camp; on 'harbour' a war pin is pushed into the ruin and Red's thread runs from its camp to the knot (RED · GAIN · A HARBOUR TO TAKE).
shots.camera: Cut close behind Red's tents, pulling back along the thread to the knot.

shots.visual: Close on Blue's camp; on 'Red' Blue's thread runs to the same knot: the first flashpoint (BLUE · FEAR · CAN'T LET RED WIN).
shots.camera: Cut close behind Blue's tents, pulling back.

shots.visual: Close on Gold's camp; on 'prince' Gold's thread runs to the knot (GOLD · A CLAIM · HIS BY BIRTH).
shots.camera: Cut close behind Gold's tents, pulling back.

shots.visual: On 'swore' a thread braided blue and gold runs between Blue's camp and Gold's (BLUE + GOLD · ALLIES · A PROMISE TO KEEP): now any move pulls all three.
shots.camera: Cut to the web from the south, pulling back.
shots.music: Muster 4: the theme on a fife, horns.

shots.purpose: Run with every side's reasons: ten years, and three armies march up to one ruin.
shots.visual: The whole Isle; YEAR 0→10; the three armies advance from their camps and stand facing the ruin; 10 YEARS / THREE ARMIES / ONE RUIN. EVERYONE'S RIGHT · 3 SIDES · 4 REASONS · 1 RUIN, stamped in lime.
shots.music: Drive with the theme; a stab and a cymbal on 'ruin'.

shots.purpose: The locked rule: nobody wants it, and it starts by mistake.
shots.visual: Dusk, close on the knot: RULE 5? NOBODY WANTS IT. On 'sure' every thread pulls taut and hums, and each side's column in the war room adds 'they'll blink' (THEY'LL BLINK); on 'wrong' the knot catches, blazing lime with a ring of light on the ground (ALL WRONG; THE FLASHPOINT · ONE WRONG GUESS), every 'they'll blink' is struck through and each verdict reads GUESSED WRONG. Nobody moves; nothing is shown fighting.
shots.camera: Cut close on the knot, then pulling back further and further as it catches.
shots.onScreenText: RULE 5? NOBODY WANTS IT · THEY'LL BLINK · ALL WRONG · THE FLASHPOINT
shots.music: Twist (a held A7♭9), then council with the clock louder.

shots.visual: Day returns, the threads slacken and the knot settles; the checklist opens and row 5 unlocks on 'cost': A GUESS · they'll back down · 5/5. The follow chip (+ FOLLOW · PART 36/50) after 'cost'.
shots.camera: The web from the south, pulling back.

layers.foreground: open checklist, follow chip, war room

shots.music: Anthem from 'So'; a D-major hit on 'cost'.

shots.visual: The full card (BEFORE YOU START A WAR · RUIN WAR, all five rows ticked) over the whole Isle in golden light, with 'Nobody thinks they're the villain.' in serif italic from the end of the first sentence.
shots.onScreenText: BEFORE YOU START A WAR · RUIN WAR · Nobody thinks they're the villain.
shots.transition: Block wipe to the end card.
shots.music: Anthem; the World Engine chime as the card lands.

shots.purpose: Comment CTA: what would finally push your kingdom into war?
shots.visual: End card: logo, PART 36 / 50, the title, and a COMMENT panel where A STOLEN HEIR and THE LAST WELL pop as starters, then 'One reason. Name it.'
shots.camera: Cut (under the block wipe) close on the knot, pulling back onto the hook pose.
shots.onScreenText: COMMENT · A STOLEN HEIR / THE LAST WELL · One reason. Name it.

graphics.title: Wars Need More Than Two Armies

shots.purpose: Say the part number, ask for the follow with a reason (part 37), open the next loop.
shots.visual: The hook frame; PART 36/50; FOLLOW FOR PART 37, pressed on 'Follow'; NEXT RUN · 37 decodes from a locked host of banners to THE BIG ARMY · TEN TIMES BIGGER. LOSING. In the world, on 'army', one grey standard far bigger than the three rises at the Isle's south-east tip and the horn calls; the Queen looks up; it sinks before the hook title returns.

layers.foreground: progress bar, follow button, next-run card

shots.onScreenText: PART 36/50 · FOLLOW FOR PART 37 · NEXT RUN: THE BIG ARMY · TEN TIMES BIGGER. LOSING.
shots.music: Tease over a held A; a horn call on 'army'; the engine chime on 'Follow'.

music.key: D minor, resolving to D major

Nobody sends a million soldiers to die for an angry king.

Meet the Ruin War: it hasn't started yet. The lazy version of a war is two armies and one angry king, and we ran it: ten years of shouting, and nobody marches. One angry king is a tantrum, not a war.

Real wars need reasons. Something to gain: Red needs the ruin's harbour. Fear: Blue can't let Red hold it. A claim: Gold's prince says it's his by birth. Allies: Blue swore to stand with Gold. Run it again: ten years, three armies, one ruin.

Then the twist: nobody here wants this war. Each side is sure the others will blink. All three are wrong. So give every side a reason worth the cost.

Show what each side wants. Nobody thinks they're the villain.

What would finally push your kingdom into war?

Part 36 of 50. Follow for part 37: big armies still lose.

Worldcraft Shorts: Worldbuilding, from the ground up. Season 2, The World Engine: every idea gets tested on one living island. Arc 8: Conflict and Warfare (the arc's first episode). The Ruin War, its three sides and their plain coloured standards are invented for this video; no real war, army, flag or nation is depicted, and nobody fights on screen.
